answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity pay a real, non-transferable cost before it can earn trust: verified work over time, staked value, or both. A fresh account starts with nothing, so an attacker cannot mint influence for free. Think of a pigment stain spreading across a tundra or cargo piling up at a wharf: the volume is visible, but without a history of honest deliveries it buys no standing. Forging thousands of credible identities would cost as much as building them honestly, which makes the attack uneconomical.
